PICO 2C: Risk of Bias: Could patient flow have introduced bias? Signaling Question 1: Was there an appropriate interval between the index test and the reference standard? The answer is no if the timing differs from this. The answer is unclear if the timing of HBV DNA testing in mothers or MTCT testing is unknown. Signaling Question 2: Did all patients in the study receive the same reference standard? The answer is yes if the markers used to assess MTCT and the timing of its assessment were consistent for all infants. Signaling Question 3: Were all patients included in the analysis? Appendix C: Data Extraction Sheet Protocol The following details are included in the data extraction sheet: Publication Details: First author, year, journal, and language. Methods: Country, main study objective, study design, recruitment period, and recruitment setting (e.g., center or regional details, number of study sites). Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria: Criteria for participant selection. Maternal HBV DNA Testing: Type of sample, timing of sample collection, type of assay (including commercial name), whether the test was qualitative or quantitative, and the limit of detection of the assay used. Maternal HBeAg Testing: Type of sample, timing of sample collection, type of assay (including commercial name), whether the test was qualitative or quantitative, and the limit of detection of the assay used. Clinical Endpoint for MTCT: Whether it was reported (Yes/No). Infant Testing: Type of sample, timing of sample collection, type of assay (including commercial name), and whether the test was qualitative or quantitative for both HBsAg and HBV DNA. Maternal antiviral therapy during pregnancy (type of drug and duration of treatment). Timing of the first dose of the HBV vaccine (timely ≤24 hours or delayed >24 hours). Administration of HBIG at birth. Completion of three doses of the hepatitis B vaccine. Participant Numbers: Number of participants at enrollment. Number of women eligible for HBsAg screening. Number of women screened for HBsAg. Number of women testing positive for HBsAg. Number of women tested for both HBV DNA and HBeAg. Number of women tested for HBV DNA. Maternal HBV DNA threshold used. Number of women with high viral load. Number of women with low viral load. Number of women screened for HBeAg. Number of women testing positive or negative for HBeAg. Women’s Characteristics: Definition of the population based on characteristics (ideally women tested for both HBV DNA and HBeAg, but often those testing positive for HBsAg). Mean (SD) or median (IQR) maternal age. Numerator/denominator by HBV viral genotypes, HIV status, HCV status, and HDV status. Outcomes 1: Sensitivity and specificity of HBeAg to diagnose high viremia. For quantitative HBV DNA tests: threshold to dichotomize into high or low viral load. For qualitative HBV DNA tests: limit of detection. Number of true positives (high viral load and HBeAg-positive). Number of false negatives (high viral load and HBeAg-negative). Number of true negatives (low viral load and HBeAg-negative). Number of false positives (low viral load and HBeAg-positive). Sensitivity of HBeAg to identify mothers with high HBV viral load. Number of women with indeterminate HBeAg results (if any). Infants’ Characteristics: Number of infants tested for HBsAg and HBV DNA at 6–12 months of age. Outcomes 2-1: Sensitivity and specificity of maternal HBeAg during pregnancy to predict MTCT (only for studies reporting MTCT endpoints). Definition of MTCT: infant HBsAg or HBV DNA, and the period in which data were collected. Number of true positives (MTCT and maternal HBeAg-positive). Number of false negatives (MTCT and maternal HBeAg-negative). Number of true negatives (no MTCT and maternal HBeAg-negative). Number of false positives (no MTCT and maternal HBeAg-positive). Sensitivity and specificity of maternal HBeAg to predict MTCT. Outcomes 2-2: Sensitivity and specificity of maternal high HBV DNA levels during pregnancy to predict MTCT (only for studies reporting MTCT endpoints). Definition of MTCT: infant HBsAg or HBV DNA, and the period in which data were collected. For quantitative HBV DNA tests: threshold to dichotomize into high or low viral load. For qualitative HBV DNA tests: limit of detection. Number of true positives (MTCT and maternal high viral load). Number of false negatives (MTCT and maternal low viral load). Number of true negatives (no MTCT and maternal low viral load). Author Contact Information: Name, affiliation, and email address of the author contacted. Questions asked to the author. Whether the author was contacted.
